question: Under an adversarial battery of poisoned interval enclosures (negative widths, NaN endpoints, non-containing enclosures) fed to interval_constants / radii_verdict, does the pipeline ever incorrectly report a closing/valid certificate?

pre_fix.note: 12 of 36 hypothesis-violating inputs were reported as CLOSING certificates, 8 of them load-bearing (the hypothesis-satisfying input of the same magnitude does NOT close). Two mechanisms: radii_verdict evaluated the discriminant on theorem-excluded constants, and interval_constants never checked the enclosure it was handed for containment.

cases.violates: H2 containment: F enclosed as exactly [0,0] at an iterate whose true residual is far from zero
cases.exception: CertificateInputError: the residual enclosure does not contain the residual: it gives Y_0 = 7.905050e-323, while F re-evaluated in float at the same point gives 5.906547e-03 in the sa

cases.violates: H2 validity AND containment: lo=+1e-16 > hi=-1e-16, and the true residual is outside
H2 validity: the honest enclosure with lo and hi exchanged (negative width, same magnitudes)
H2 validity: a NaN endpoint in component 0 of the residual enclosure

verdict.reason: INVALID_INPUT: outside the hypotheses of the radii polynomial theorem (Y_0, Z_1, Z_2 are upper bounds on norms, hence finite and nonnegative): Y_0 is NaN (a norm bound cannot be NaN; note that `NaN < 1.0` is False, so the contraction guard alone is not a hypothesis check). No discriminant is evaluated.
